title: Renewal Health — Token Audit & Spend Diagnostics
content:
Purpose:
To give Customer Success and Renewal teams a compact, repeatable worksheet for QBRs that diagnoses token spend drivers, exposes rate-limit and quota pressure, and recommends immediate mitigations and renewal talking points. Use this during the 30/90-day renewal sprint to assess risk and propose concrete cost/usage actions.

How to use (1-page guide):
- Populate the Token-Burn-Metrics tab with last 90 days of token usage broken down by: total_tokens, unique_active_users, calls_per_minute_peak, avg_tokens_per_call, model_variant.
- Populate Rate-Limit-Incidents with any observed 429/5xx spikes, timestamps, endpoints impacted.
- Run the Diagnostic Checks (section below) to auto-flag anomalies.
- Draft QBR talking points from the QBR-Talking-Points tab; assign owners in Action-Plan.

Key diagnostic metrics (include raw numbers in Token-Burn-Metrics):
- 30d_total_tokens: total tokens used in last 30 days.
- 30d_token_burn_per_user = 30d_total_tokens / unique_active_users_30d.
- 7d_growth_rate = (tokens_day_0 - tokens_day_7) / tokens_day_7 (expressed as %).
- peak_rps = highest requests/sec observed in 30d bucket.
- avg_tokens_per_call (tokens / total_calls).
- cost_per_1k_tokens = billing_rate * 1000 (pull from billing export).

Simple risk bands (suggested thresholds — tune per customer):
- Green (Low risk): 30d_total_tokens < 50k OR 30d_token_burn_per_user < 150; no rate limit incidents.
- Yellow (Medium risk): 50k <= 30d_total_tokens < 250k OR 30d_token_burn_per_user between 150-750; 1-2 rate-limit incidents.
- Red (High risk): 30d_total_tokens >= 250k OR 30d_token_burn_per_user > 750 OR repeated rate-limit incidents or >20% 7d_growth_rate.

Diagnostic checks (manual or scripted):
1) Sudden-growth check: If any 7d_growth_rate > 20% -> flag for growth spike.
2) Hot-user check: Sort users by tokens; if top 5 users account for >50% of tokens -> investigate automation or bot traffic.
3) Cost shock check: Calculate last invoice vs projected burn. If projected monthly cost > invoice by >25% -> escalate to FinOps.
4) Latency-induced retries check: Correlate 5xx/timeout windows with doubled token burn (retries).
5) Model change check: If model variant changed in last 30d and avg_tokens_per_call shifted by >30% -> ask engineering for rollout notes.

Rate-limit and quota review (what to capture in sheet):
- Route/endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings)
- Configured rate limit (rps) and burst allowance
- Observed throttled requests (count)
- Time windows of throttling with UTC timestamps
- Business impact note (e.g., "checkout flow slowed; browser retries visible")

Budget alert templates (copyable strings for internal alerting and customer emails):
- Internal Slack alert (ops): "ALERT: {customer} projected monthly token spend exceeded threshold: projected ${proj} vs commit ${commit}. Review usage drivers and enable interim throttles or quota guardrails."
- Customer-facing FYI: "Heads up — your usage is trending above our initial projection. We recommend reviewing your most active endpoints and considering quota rules to avoid unexpected billing. Can we schedule a 30-min runbook call?"
- Escalation trigger: "If projected spend > commit by 30% or if rate-limit incidents > 3 in 7d -> escalate to AM + Solutions Eng."

QBR talking points (auto-fill examples — edit for each account):
- "Summary: Last 30 days token consumption = 184k (avg daily = 6.1k). Growth driven by new onboarding flow (model=gpt-base-16k) which increased avg_tokens_per_call from 420 -> 920."
- "Risk: Two rounds of transient throttling observed on 2026-01-18 and 2026-01-23 during peak US hours. Impacted checkout flow; retries observed in frontend logs."
- "Opportunity: Enable prefix-caching on chat endpoint and add a soft quota for non-paying test tenants; estimated 18-25% token savings."
- "Ask: Approve 30-min runbook with Solutions Eng to tune batching and caching prior to renewal; consider a supplemental 2-week commit to cover projected burst."

Action plan template (columns to capture in Action-Plan tab):
- Action ID (short)
- Description (one line)
- Owner (name)
- Priority (P0/P1/P2)
- ETA (date)
- Status (todo/in_progress/done)
- Impact estimate (tokens/month or $/month)

Sample entries to copy: 
- A1 | "Enable 30s KV prefix cache on /chat" | Marcus Green | P0 | 2026-02-28 | in_progress | ~15% token reduction
- A2 | "Add soft quota for staging tenants" | Lena Cho | P1 | 2026-03-05 | todo | reduces burst risk
- A3 | "Investigate top-5 hot users" | Customer Success | P0 | 2026-02-24 | todo | isolates automation-driven usage

Renewal risk score (suggested formula — convert to 0-100):
- Base = 50
- +15 if 7d_growth_rate > 10%
- +20 if repeated rate-limit incidents in last 30d (>2)
- +10 if projected monthly spend > commit by 15%
- -10 if agreed optimization actions in place and tracked as in_progress/done
- Interpretation: score < 40 = low churn risk; 40-65 = monitor; >65 = high risk, sales/AM intervention required.

Data export checklist (for engineering/CS handoff):
- Billing export (CSV): token-level cost and model mapping for last 90d.
- Request logs (sample): include request_id, timestamp, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant.
- Rate-limit logs: 429s with timestamps and client identifiers.
- Frontend retry traces for suspected retries (to rule out doubled burn).

Meeting preparation (QBR):
- Pre-read for AM/Customer: 1-page summary (top-line metrics + risk band + 2 recommended actions).
- Agenda: 1) Health snapshot 2) Root-cause of any anomalies 3) Actions (timelines + owners) 4) Renewal implications and options (commit bump, safety cap, short-term top-up).
- Attachments to share: billing export + 7d per-hour token burn chart + rate-limit incident timeline.

Notes to CS team (best-practices nuggets):
- Always call out automation vs organic growth. The top-10 user breakdown is the first signal for automation.
- Use a combined "cost + availability" framing when suggesting short-term top-ups. Customers accept temporary commit increases to avoid user-facing throttles.
- Convert technical mitigations into customer-facing outcomes ("reduces monthly bill by ~x%" or "eliminates retry-induced errors").

Open questions to resolve during audit: 
- Has the customer changed model_variant or prompt templates in the last 60 days?
- Are there scheduled marketing campaigns or rollouts that could increase peak RPS?
- Does the customer have a separate non-prod tenant that is not rate-limited?

Checklist for post-QBR follow-up (copy into Action-Plan):
- [ ] Share annotated billing export with customer.
- [ ] Confirm owners for A1-A3.
- [ ] Set internal alert threshold for projected spend +20%.
- [ ] Schedule runbook call within 7 days if score > 65.

End of worksheet. Keep this sheet attached to every renewal packet for consistency. If you want, we can add a small script to populate the Token-Burn-Metrics tab from the billing export — tag CS infra for automation.
